name: Lancelot
summary: A fast V-22-class tiltrotor medic that beats the golden hour to any point in range, lands vertically with no runway, and carries a patient and medic.
description: EX-1 Lancelot is an Efficient-class expeditionary craft (EX — E for Efficient, X for expeditionary craft; the fleet is Expeditionary). It is the fleet’s fast medical first responder: a tiltrotor that beats the golden hour to any point in range, takes off and lands vertically with no runway, and carries a patient and an attending medic in a dedicated medical module. If a patient cannot be moved, it holds position until heavier help (VX-11 George) arrives.

calculations.title: Hover power
calculations.method: Momentum theory at MTOW, FM 0.72, disc area from R 5.75 m × 2.
calculations.note: Disk loading 567 N/m², well below V-22’s ~1,110 — gentler downwash.

calculations.title: Cruise power
calculations.method: P = W·V/(L/D·η_prop), L/D 9, η_p 0.80 at MTOW.

blueprint.frame: X=0 at nose tip, +X aft; Y=0 centreline; Z=0 centreline. Fuselage 18.0 m × 2.6 m × 2.4 m.
blueprint.stations: Cockpit 0–3.5 m (pilot+medic tandem); fwd systems 3.5–5.5; modular bay 5.5–11.5 (low-slung); wing carry-through + fuel 11.5–14.5; aft systems + tail 14.5–18.0.
blueprint.notes: High wing at Z +1.2→+1.6; bay keel bulges to Z −1.6; rotor plane VTOL ≈ +2.4.

sections.heading: The EX-1 / EX-2 pair
sections.body: EX-1 and EX-2 are one airframe in two roles — the clearest expression of the adaptability principle. The Lancelot is the fast, light medic (12 t, Mach 0.75 dash); the Gawain is the heavier hover-dominated hauler (17 t, 5 t lift). They share wing, nacelles, rotor geometry, and module interface; they differ in gauge, engine rating, and payload.

sections.heading: Design philosophy
sections.body: Efficiency, Adaptability (one airframe, swappable modules), and Reliability (engine cross-shafting so a single failure is survivable — either rotor can be driven if one engine is lost).

decisions.why: One design/build/maintain for two missions — efficiency and adaptability.
